svg.title: PNP P033 walkthrough — Products that have never been ordered
svg.desc: Products catalogue, LEFT JOIN to OrderDetails, unmatched-row filter and final anti-join output.
svg.text: Which catalogue products have no order line?
Follow Products 1–2 through the LEFT JOIN and unmatched-row filter.
ƒ = calculated/test field · ▸ = focus row · double underline = join key
FROM Products supplies the complete catalogue because the report must find products with no order history as
well as products with matches. Starting from OrderDetails would lose never-ordered products before they could
Why add OrderDetails with a LEFT JOIN?
ProductID is already available from each Products row, so OrderDetails can be added on Products.ProductID =
OrderDetails.ProductID. LEFT JOIN keeps every catalogue product: Pen matches order-detail row 10; Cup has no
Why keep only OD.OrderDetailID IS NULL?
OrderDetailID is the non-null primary key of a real order line. NULL therefore marks a Products row with no
match. Pen is removed because it matched row 10; Cup survives because its green right-side key is NULL.
If Pen had two order lines, the LEFT JOIN would repeat Pen twice; both matched rows would be removed.
Why does Cup become the final output row?
The locked query returns the five requested Products fields and sorts by CategoryID, then ProductID,
ascending. The anti-join removes every product with at least one order-detail match and keeps each unmatched
Final: 2 catalogue products checked · 1 matched product removed · 1 never-ordered product retained
Source key: blue = Products · green = OrderDetails · purple = the derived match test.
